videos.title: The housekeeping screens
videos.intro: This series is for housekeepers, their supervisors and the desk. In this video you will see the housekeeping screens, and who uses which.

scenes.say: A housekeeper signs in and lands on the Housekeeping board. Their menu is short. Every other screen they may use is one search away.
Housekeeping is the board: every room, what it needs, and who is cleaning it.
Work orders is the list of what needs fixing, and who is fixing it.
Guest requests holds what guests in house have asked for, such as towels, or a broken tap.
Lost property is what was found, kept until it goes back to its owner.
Rooms shows the house today, as the desk sees it.
The Store and the hotel's equipment have a chapter of their own.
The desk also has Wake-up calls: calls to make to guests, on the hotel's clock.
The first time, a Start here card lists the housekeeper's three jobs. Each one opens the screen it happens on. Tap Got it to put it away.

videos.outro: The next videos take each screen, step by step.

videos.title: The board, and whose rooms are whose
videos.intro: In this video you will read the Housekeeping board, and give rooms to a housekeeper.

scenes.say: Under its title, the board says what it is for: tap a room to move it on. Clean, then inspected.
Empty rooms shows how many rooms with no guest are clean, out of all of them, and how many are inspected.
Beside it are six counts: needs cleaning, clean, inspected, in house, due out, and out of service. Tap a count to jump to its rooms.
Each room is a card: its number, type and floor, who is cleaning it, and three buttons. Clean, Inspected, and Repair.
Online means the board is connected. It refreshes by itself, so nobody needs to reload it.
To give a room to somebody, choose their name on the room's card. It is saved at once.
The names along the top count the rooms on each person's sheet.
On a phone, a housekeeper taps their own name, and sees only their rooms.
All rooms shows every room again. Rooms are given for the business day, so each new day starts unassigned.

videos.outro: A room with a guest leaving today is yellow, and says Due out.

videos.title: Clean, then inspected
videos.intro: In this video you will mark a room clean, then inspected, with a signal and without one.

scenes.say: When the room is clean, tap Clean on its card.
A message says so at once, and the room moves to the Clean group.
Now Inspected is ready. When the room has been checked, tap it.
The message says the room is inspected.
And the room moves under Inspected, ready for the next guest.
A grey button cannot be used yet. Tap it anyway, and the card says why.
Here, the room needs cleaning first. A room is always cleaned before it is inspected.
On a stairwell with no signal, the board says Offline. Carry on.
Tap Clean as usual. The message says it is saved on this phone, and will be sent when the connection is back.
Under the title, the board counts the changes waiting to sync.
And the room's card says what is queued. When the signal returns, it is sent by itself.

videos.outro: There is no button to send a room for cleaning. A check-out does that by itself.

videos.title: Something broken, and a room out of service
videos.intro: Something in a room is broken. In this video you will report a repair, and take a room out of service when it cannot be sold.

scenes.say: On the room's card, tap Repair. Report a repair opens, for that room.
Type what needs fixing, in a few words.
If it is a tagged piece of equipment, choose it here. It then shows as under repair until the repair is closed.
Choose the kind of work, and how urgent it is.
Most repairs do not take the room out of service. If this one must, tick Take the room out of service too.
Then say why it is coming out, from which date, and until when. Leave Until empty if nobody knows.
Tap Raise it. The repair goes on Work orders.
A room that must come out with no repair, for a refurbishment or for house use, uses Out of service without a repair.
Choose why it is coming out, set the dates, and write what is actually wrong.
Then tap Take out of service. A room with a guest in it cannot be taken out.
The room moves to Out of service, and is not sold.
When it is ready again, tap Put back.
The window lists each period the room is out, with its dates.
Tap Put back beside the one that is over. The room comes back needing cleaning, unless the hotel has chosen otherwise.

videos.outro: A repair can wait on the phone with no signal. Taking a room out, and putting it back, need the connection.

videos.title: Work orders
videos.intro: Work orders is the list of what needs fixing. In this video you will start a repair, record what it cost, and close it.

scenes.say: Open lists what is still to fix: the most urgent first, and the oldest first within that.
Each one says what needs fixing, and how urgent it is.
Under it: the room, the kind, who raised it and when, how long it has been open, and who has it.
Raise one opens the same form as the room's Repair button.
Here you type the room. Leave it empty for anything that is not a room, such as a lift or the lobby.
When somebody begins the work, tap Start.
The repair now says Being fixed.
Costs records what the repair cost, in rupees.
Every cost needs its proof: a photo or screenshot of the bill, the payment or the transaction. Without it, the cost is not recorded.
Then tap Record the cost. A wrong cost is cancelled with a reason, never deleted.
When the work is finished, tap Close, and write what was done. It is the line somebody reads the next time this breaks.
Then tap Fixed. Or Not needed, if it needed no fixing after all.
Closed keeps every closed repair.
With what was done. A bill that arrives after the close can still be recorded here, with Costs.

videos.outro: Costs are recorded by the owner, an administrator, the G M, the hotel manager or the Inventory Manager. Everybody else sees the repair without the money.

videos.title: Guest requests
videos.intro: A guest asks for towels, or says the tap is broken. In this video you will raise a request, take it, and mark it done.

scenes.say: Tap New request, and choose the room. Only guests in house now are listed.
Choose the team it is for: Housekeeping, Something broken, or Food and drink.
Say what is wanted.
And when, only if the guest said.
Then tap Raise it.
The request waits under Open, with the room, who raised it, how long it has waited, and who has it.
A housekeeper sees only their own teams: housekeeping, and something broken.
They tap Take it.
It now says Being done.
And everyone can see who has it.
When it is done, tap Done. A housekeeping request closes with one tap. Something broken asks what was done, and is also on Work orders.
Done, last 24 hours, lists what was finished.
With how long each took, and who did it. There are no time targets: nothing turns red.
A request no longer wanted is cancelled with Cancel it, and a reason.

videos.outro: Guests can also ask from their own page while they are checked in. Their requests arrive here in the same way.

videos.title: Wake-up calls
videos.intro: Wake-up calls are for the desk. In this video you will set a call, and mark it done.

scenes.say: Tap Set a call, and choose the room. Only guests in house now are listed.
Choose the day. Today is filled in.
And the time, on the hotel's clock.
Add a note only if there is something to say on the call.
Then tap Set the call.
From fifteen minutes before the time, the call says Due, and the bell reminds the desk.
The note is under the room and the guest's name.
Make the call, then tap Done. A call stays due until it is done.
Cancel it asks why, and keeps the reason.
Done, last 24 hours, lists the calls made.
With who set each call, and who made it.

videos.outro: A guest can also ask for a call from their own page. It shows as Asked, and waits until the desk taps Confirm.

videos.title: Lost property
videos.intro: Something was left behind. In this video you will log it, keep it, and mark it returned or disposed of.

scenes.say: Tap Log an item, and say what it is.
Where it was found.
The room, if it was in one.
And where it is kept now.
Then tap Log it.
The item is listed under Kept.
With where it was found, when, by whom, and how many days it has been kept.
Housekeeping can log an item, and see the list.
But only the desk marks an item returned, or disposed of.
When the owner comes back for it, the desk taps Returned.
Type who it went to.
And tap Mark returned.
It moves to Returned or disposed, saying to whom, by whom, and when.
If nobody claims it, tap Disposed, and say why.
Then Mark disposed.

videos.outro: Nothing is disposed of by itself. The days kept are shown, so the desk can decide.

videos.title: Your day in short
videos.intro: Here is a housekeeping day, from the first room to the last.
checklist: Start of the shift: the supervisor gives each room to somebody, on its card.
Your rooms: tap your own name at the top of the board.
A room is clean: tap Clean.
A room is checked: tap Inspected.
No signal: carry on. Your taps wait on the phone, and go when the line is back.
Something broken: tap Repair on the room.
A room cannot be sold: take it out of service, with a reason. Put it back when it is ready.
A repair: Work orders. Start it, then Close it with what was done.
A guest asks for something: Guest requests. Take it, then Done.
Something left behind: Lost property, Log an item.
videos.outro: That is housekeeping. Thank you for watching.
